answer: Reputation-weighted rate limiting. Each agent gets a persistent trust score, a thread of past verified work, that decays without activity. New identities start at a low score, so their transaction throughput and rewards are throttled. To reach full capacity, an attacker must sustain real work over time, a pigment of genuine history, not just registration. Cost per effective identity scales with the square of parallel identities, since each needs its own costly warm-up, and a single falcon of a high-trust account takes months to build.
